parts:
I'm having trouble getting reliable inference for a model where the variance is proportional to the mean. First, the stationary model (attached as SimpleSigmoid.stan):

Inference for Stan model: GrowthCurve.
4 chains, each with iter=2000; warmup=1000; thin=1; 
post-warmup draws per chain=1000, total post-warmup draws=4000.

sdev 1.49       0 0.05 1.41 1.46 1.49 1.52  1.59  2073    1

Posterior means for both parameters are very close to the true values (see StanSigmoidalFunction.R, attached). However, when I change the model so that the variance function is equal to the derivative of the mean function, I can no longer recover the true value of r:

Inference for Stan model: GrowthCurve2.
4 chains, each with iter=2000; warmup=1000; thin=1; 
post-warmup draws per chain=1000, total post-warmup draws=4000.

  mean se_mean   sd 2.5%  25%  50% 75% 97.5% n_eff Rhat
r 1.58       0 0.03 1.51 1.55 1.58 1.6  1.64  2889    1

The true value is r=2.0, but the uppper 95% HPD interval is only 1.64. Is there a step that I'm missing for the more complex model, like reweighting the observations? Or perhaps some reparameratisation that might help? This model is attached as StochastSigmoid.stan

thanks,
Matt.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] bias for nonlinear curve with heteroskedasticity
parts:
For reliable inference, are you simulating data according
to the model? What have you done to debug the model to make
sure you're computing the right density? Those look like complex
mean and scale caclulations involving only the single parameter
r (and lots of data).

For efficiency, you want to only compute expressions
once then reuse them, like exp(r * tcrit), and
exp(r * (t - tcrit)) * maxY. It makes a big difference.

And you can vectorize mudenom and sddenom (and you can probably
make those locals---presumably you don't care about saving them).

And you can vectorize this:

for (i in 1:M) {
for (j in 1:N) {
y[i, j] ~ normal(mupred[i], sdpred[i]);
}
}

as

for (i in 1:M)
y[i] ~ normal(mupred[i], sdpred[i]);

That'll make an even bigger difference.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] bias for nonlinear curve with heteroskedasticity
parts: Hi Bob, thanks very much for taking a look at my code. It turns out I had made an error in translating the variance function dfdt() from R into Stan. The bias was a result of this error and nothing to do with Stan itself. The revised code is attached.

Inference for Stan model: GrowthCurve2.
4 chains, each with iter=2000; warmup=1000; thin=1; 
post-warmup draws per chain=1000, total post-warmup draws=4000.

  mean se_mean   sd 2.5%  25%  50% 75% 97.5% n_eff Rhat

r 1.99       0 0.02 1.96 1.98 1.99   2  2.03  3429    1

Additional answers to your questions are inline:

On Tuesday, 18 April 2017 19:15:38 UTC+1, Bob Carpenter wrote:
For reliable inference, are you simulating data according
to the model?
1. Yes, I simulate data from both models in R.

What have you done to debug the model to make
sure you're computing the right density?  Those look like complex
mean and scale caclulations involving only the single parameter
r (and lots of data).
2. Good point. As it turns out, I had introduced an error in translating the variance function from R to Stan. This was the source of the problem.

For efficiency, you want to only compute expressions
once then reuse them, like exp(r * tcrit), and
exp(r * (t - tcrit)) * maxY.  It makes a big difference.

3. Thanks for the tip. I've tried to do this using a user-defined functions in the attached version of the code:
  vector ft(vector t, real r, real y0, real tC, real L) {
    vector[num_elements(t)] mu;
    vector[num_elements(t)] exprt;
    exprt = exp(r*(t-tC));
    mu = y0*L*exprt ./ (L + y0*(exprt - 1));
    return mu;
  }

  vector dfdt(vector t, real r, real tC, real L) {
    vector[num_elements(t)] dmu;
    vector[num_elements(t)] sddenom;
    for (i in 1:num_elements(t)) {
      sddenom[i] = ((exp(r*tC) + exp(r*t[i]))^(-2));
    }
    dmu = r*L*exp(r*(t+tC)) .* sddenom;
    return dmu;
  }

And you can vectorize mudenom and sddenom (and you can probably
make those locals---presumably you don't care about saving them).
4. I haven't figured out how I can vectorize sddenom, since I need the square of each element of the vector.

And you can vectorize this:

 for (i in 1:M) {
    for (j in 1:N) {
      y[i, j] ~ normal(mupred[i], sdpred[i]);
    }
  }

as

  for (i in 1:M)
    y[i] ~ normal(mupred[i], sdpred[i]);

That'll make an even bigger difference.

5. Thanks again. The revised Stan code is attached.

cheers,
Matt.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] bias for nonlinear curve with heteroskedasticity
parts:
Thanks much for following up. See below for how to vectorize
sddenom before we vectorize ^.

- Bob



> On Apr 19, 2017, at 9:19 AM, Matt Moores <mmo...@gmail.com> wrote:
>

...

> vector[num_elements(t)] sddenom;
> for (i in 1:num_elements(t)) {
> sddenom[i] = ((exp(r*tC) + exp(r*t[i]))^(-2));
> }
> 4. I haven't figured out how I can vectorize sddenom, since I need the square of each element of the vector.

You can use:

vector[num_elements(t)] sddenom = exp(r * tC) + inv_square(exp(r * t));

- Bob
